Definition: from G1199; a captive (as bound):--in bonds, prisoner.
BiblicalUsage: A prisoner in bonds is someone held fast by chains, and Paul uses the word of himself more than anyone. He calls himself the prisoner of the Lord in Ephesians and the prisoner of Christ Jesus in his letter to Philemon, and he asks the churches to remember those in bonds as if bound with them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul turned his chains into a pulpit. He was a prisoner of Rome, but he called himself the prisoner of Christ, and that naming of his master is what made his bonds a witness instead of a shame.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
